cases.name: Savannah Spurlock
cases.about:
In the years since Spurlock disappeared, her loved ones have made sure to keep her memory alive for her four children.

“There's pictures, there's blankets, songs, or Christmas ornaments,” Speratos said. “Every now and then we will take them to the gravesite … she's there, most importantly she's there for them.”
cases.narrative:
On 7/10/2019, her body was found buried, wrapped in plastic bags in a 19-inch deep in a clandestine grave on Sparks’ family’s Garrard County farm. Her feet were bound with tape, her body was folded over and a rug was behind her back.

Sparks’ father was digging in a strawberry patch on the family farm when he uncovered something that had a strong odor. When investigators arrived, they uncovered Spurlock’s body.

The amount of time Spurlock’s body was buried destroyed any evidence for medical examiners to use to determine what caused her death, the medical examiner wrote.

Savannah disappeared after leaving a bar in Lexington with three men, one of whom was David Sparks.

cases.name: Bronwyn Athea "Thea" Wilson
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Bronwyn was a fearless and active child who decided at age 5 she no longer wanted to go by a nickname (Thea). She got quite testy until Bronwyn became the official name.

Bronwyn shared a love of true crime and true tales of ghosts and the paranormal. She had an unending love of seafood, sharing this with her paternal aunt, Rebecca Wilson. She loved cooking, baking, decorating cakes, and more. Her favorite time of year was Halloween, and some of her makeup creations for trick or treat were shockingly realistic. She was a lover of many kinds of pets, including cats, ferrets, rats, rabbits and goldfish.

Bronwyn made friends wherever she went. All of them miss her deeply."

cases.name: Bryonny Allison Wilson
cases.about:
She worked with the Lexington Public Library. Bronwyn was a cake decorator at Mondelli’s Bakeshop.

Her obituary said, "She was employed by the Lexington Public Library for many years, beginning in the page position at the Eagle Creek Branch nearly 17 years ago, then becoming a Children's Associate at the Central Library. Later she was promoted again to a full-time Cataloging Specialist position and was responsible for entering all children's books in the library cataloging system. She also used her artistic talent to do many signs and displays for the library.

Bry loved reading and playing Animal Crossings. She also loved steampunk and had several amazing pieces in her collection. She adored her cats and shared a love of Halloween with her mother and sister. They would decorate every year, decking out the house and buying cauldrons of candy. Bry was very serious, even when young, but she had her silly side, and was generous with her laughter to those left behind."

cases.name: Lisa Lynn Wand Wilson
cases.about:
Toni Spicer, one of Lisa’s former coworkers, said Lisa made her patients laugh as they worked toward recovery. Spicer said Lisa was the provider of her family, working long shifts to support her daughters and husband. Spicer said Steven Wilson stayed at home and drove his family members to work and gatherings. She was retired but had been a registered nurse at Good Samaritan Hospital.

Her obituary said, "Lisa Wilson grew up wanting to emulate her mother and follow her into the nursing profession. She was a Candy Striper volunteer at Central Baptist Hospital and later received her RN degree at her mother's alma mater, Deaconess School of Nursing in Evansville, Indiana. Lisa spent nearly her entire career working at Good Samaritan Hospital, now part of the University of Kentucky Healthcare system.

Unfortunately, she contracted the Covid virus before vaccines were available. This impact on her health influenced her decision to retire early. However, her life was cut short and she was unable to enjoy life in retirement.

Lisa is sorely missed by her coworkers at Samaritan, several of whom have shared stories of how Lisa inspired or supported them in their work. She especially saw to it that her unit at the hospital was well-supplied with chocolate.

Lisa is deeply missed by her extended family, along with her daughters Bryonny (Bry) and Bronwyn Wilson, who accompanied her in death."
